docs.title: Getting started
docs.summary: Install FIFU, paste an image URL into a post, and publish your first remote featured image in a few minutes.

illustration.caption: Four steps to your first remote featured image: install FIFU, paste the image URL, check the preview, and publish.
illustration.alt: Four steps: the FIFU plugin with an Activate button, the FIFU box with an image URL and a Preview button, the FIFU box showing the image preview, and the published post showing the image.

facts.label: Works with
facts.value: Posts, pages, custom post types, and WooCommerce

blocks.text: **Featured Image from URL (FIFU)** lets you use an image that lives on another website as the featured image of your posts, pages, custom post types, and WooCommerce products. You paste the image address, and WordPress shows the image straight from where it's stored.
The image is **not downloaded** to your Media Library. That brings a few nice benefits:

items: **Less storage.** Your site doesn't keep a copy of every image.
**Faster setup and imports.** There's nothing to upload or process.
**Works with your theme.** Themes and plugins that show featured images can show FIFU images too.

items.title: In WordPress, go to [[Plugins]] › [[Add New Plugin]].
Search for **Featured Image from URL** (or **FIFU**).
Click [[Install Now]], then [[Activate]].

blocks.text: Prefer to install by hand? Upload the `featured-image-from-url` folder to `/wp-content/plugins/` and activate FIFU from the [[Plugins]] screen.

blocks.title: A new menu appears
blocks.text: After activation you'll see **FIFU** (with a camera icon) in the left admin menu. It contains [[Settings]], [[Cloud]], and [[Status]].

items.title: Open a post, page, or product for editing.
Find the **FIFU** box in the editor sidebar.
items.text: In the block editor it's on the [[Post]] (or [[Page]]) tab of the right sidebar.

items.title: Paste the image address into the [[Image URL or Keywords]] field.
items.text: For example: `https://example.com/photos/beach.jpg`.

items.title: Click [[Preview]].
items.text: If the image appears, the address works.

items.title: Optionally fill in [[Alternative text]].
items.text: It describes the image for screen readers and search engines.

items.title: Click [[Save]], [[Update]], or [[Publish]], then view your post.

blocks.text: Most problems come from the address itself. A good image address:

items: starts with `https://` (or `http://`) and includes the full domain;
points **directly to the image file**, often ending in `.jpg`, `.png`, or `.webp`, not to a web page that contains the image;
is **public**, so it opens without logging in;
comes from a site that allows its images to be shown on other websites.

blocks.title: Quick test
blocks.text: Open the address in a private browser window. If you see only the image, it will work with FIFU.
Share links from Google Drive and OneDrive are converted for you. See [Featured image from URL](/docs/featured-image-from-url/) for details.

items: Show an image on posts that don't have one: [Default Featured Image](/docs/default-featured-image/).
Let FIFU pick the first image of each post: [Auto set featured media from post content](/docs/auto-set-featured-media-from-post-content/).
Edit many images quickly from the post list: [Quick Editor and content lists](/docs/quick-editor/).
Use remote images in your store: [Product and category images](/docs/product-and-category-images/).

blocks.text: The [[Help]] tab of FIFU's settings has a [[Technical support]] section with the support email, `support@fifu.app`. When you write, include your site's status summary so the team can understand your setup. The [Status page](/docs/status-page/) guide shows how to copy it.

docs.title: Featured image from URL
docs.summary: Use the FIFU box in the post editor to set a featured image and its alternative text from any public image URL.

illustration.caption: You fill in the FIFU box in the editor; your site shows the image straight from its original address.
illustration.alt: On the left, the FIFU box with Featured image selected, an image preview with a remove button, alternative text, and the image URL. On the right, the published post showing the same image.

locations.label: Also in
path: Pages, products, and custom post types

facts.label: Available for
facts.value: Every content type that supports featured images

blocks.text: FIFU adds a box called **FIFU** (with a camera icon) to the editor of every content type that supports featured images: posts, pages, WooCommerce products, and custom post types.

items: **Block editor:** open the right sidebar and look on the [[Post]] or [[Page]] tab.
**Classic editor:** the box sits in the right column, near WordPress's own featured image box.

blocks.text: At the top of the box, a menu shows [[Featured image]]. That's the type you'll use. The other types in the menu show a lock icon.

sections.title: Add an image from a URL

items.title: Paste the image address into [[Image URL or Keywords]].
Click [[Preview]].
items.text: FIFU loads the image to make sure it works and shows it in the box.

items.title: Type a description in [[Alternative text]].
Save or update the post.

blocks.text: After you click [[Preview]] you'll see one of these:

items: **The image.** Everything is fine.
**An “image not found” picture.** The address can't be loaded. Check that it's complete, public, and points to the image file.
**A photo search window.** You typed words instead of an address, so FIFU searched Unsplash. See [Unsplash image search](/docs/unsplash-image-search/).

blocks.title: Need examples?
blocks.text: Click the small image icon at the left of the field ([[Image URL help]]) to see example addresses and keywords.
Alternative text describes the image for people who use screen readers and helps search engines understand it. Write a short, plain description, such as “Sunset over a calm beach”.
If you leave [[Alternative text]] empty, **FIFU uses the post title automatically**, so your image always has a description.

items: **To remove** the image, click the **×** button on the preview ([[Remove featured image]]), then save the post.
**To change** it, remove the current image, paste the new address, click [[Preview]], and save.

blocks.title: WordPress's own featured image panel
blocks.text: While a post has a FIFU image, the block editor hides the regular [[Featured image]] panel to avoid confusion. Remove the FIFU image and it comes back, so you can choose an image from the Media Library again. When Rank Math is active, both panels stay visible.
Some services give you a link to a page, not to the image itself. FIFU fixes these automatically:

items: **Google Drive** share links (`drive.google.com`) become direct image links.
**OneDrive** short links (`1drv.ms`) become direct image links.

blocks.title: Share the file publicly
blocks.text: On Google Drive and OneDrive, set the file to “Anyone with the link”. Private files can't be shown to your visitors.

items: The image stays on its original server. If that server removes or moves it, it disappears from your site. [Replace Not Found Image](/docs/replace-not-found-image/) can show a backup image when that happens.
The box works the same way for pages, WooCommerce products, and custom post types.
If the **Sirv** plugin is active, a [[Choose Sirv image]] button appears next to [[Preview]] so you can pick an image from your Sirv account.

docs.title: Unsplash image search
docs.summary: Type keywords instead of a URL to search Unsplash and pick a free photo as your featured image.

illustration.caption: Type keywords instead of a URL, pick a photo from the results, and it becomes the featured image.
illustration.alt: Three steps: the FIFU box with the keywords sun,sea and the Preview button, a grid of photo results with one selected, and the FIFU box showing the chosen photo and its Unsplash address.

blocks.text: The field where you paste an image address also accepts **keywords**. When you type words instead of an address, FIFU searches **Unsplash**, a large library of free, high-quality photos, and shows the results in a window. Click a photo and its address is placed in the field for you.
The photo isn't downloaded. Like any FIFU image, it's shown from its original address.

items.title: In the **FIFU** box, type one or more keywords into [[Image URL or Keywords]].
items.text: Separate keywords with commas, for example `sun,sea`.

items.title: Click [[Preview]].
items.text: A window opens with matching photos.

items.title: Scroll to see more.
items.text: New photos load as you reach the bottom.

items.title: Click the photo you like.
items.text: Its address goes into the field and the preview appears.

items.title: Add [[Alternative text]] and save the post.

blocks.text: The same search works in the [Quick Editor](/docs/quick-editor/). Click a post's image in the list, type keywords into [[Image URL or Keywords]], and click [[Preview]]. Pick a photo, then click [[Save]].

items: Use one to three specific words, like `coffee,cup` instead of `drink`.
If a search in your language returns few photos, try English words.
If nothing appears, try broader or different words.
The search needs at least one keyword. An empty field doesn't start a search.

blocks.text: Searching requires permission to upload files. By default that includes **Administrators**, **Editors**, and **Authors**. **Contributors** can't run searches.

blocks.title: About the photos
blocks.text: Photos on Unsplash are free to use under the Unsplash License. Crediting the photographer isn't required, but it's appreciated.

docs.title: Quick Editor and content lists
docs.summary: Preview, replace, or remove featured images right from your list of posts, and filter the list by image status.

illustration.caption: Change images right from the list: click a thumbnail, paste a URL or keywords, and save. The status menu finds posts without images.
illustration.alt: The All Posts list with the All featured media statuses menu and a FIFU column of thumbnails, one of them clicked. Next to it, the Quick edit window with an image preview, the image URL, alternative text, and the Clear and Save buttons.

facts.label: Lists
facts.value: Posts, pages, products, product categories, and custom post types

blocks.text: FIFU adds a column with a camera icon to your content lists, such as [[All Posts]], [[Pages]], and [[Products]]. Hover over the icon and its tooltip reads [[Quick edit]]. Each row shows a thumbnail of the featured image, whether it comes from a URL or from the Media Library. The same column appears in [[Products]] › [[Categories]].

blocks.title: Hide the column
blocks.text: Open [[Screen Options]] at the top of the list and uncheck **FIFU** if you don't need the column on a screen.

sections.title: Change an image without opening the post

items.title: Click the thumbnail (or the empty square) in the FIFU column.
items.text: The Quick Editor opens for that item.

items.title: Type an image address, or keywords, into [[Image URL or Keywords]] and click [[Preview]].
items.text: Keywords open the [Unsplash image search](/docs/unsplash-image-search/).

items.title: Fill in [[Alternative text]] if you like.
Click [[Save]].
items.text: The thumbnail in the list updates.

items.label: Clear
items.text: Empties the fields so you can start again.

items.label: Remove remote image
items.text: The **×** button on the preview removes the featured image. Click [[Save]] to confirm.

blocks.text: Above the list of posts, pages, products, or custom post types, FIFU adds a menu called [[All featured media statuses]]. Choose an option and click [[Filter]]:

rows: Items that have a featured image of any kind.
Items without a featured image. Great for finding what's missing.
Items whose image comes from a URL through FIFU.
Items whose image comes from your Media Library.

items: The column and the filter are available to users who can publish posts. Category lists have the column, but not the filter.
In the Quick Editor, [[Featured image]] is the only media type you can use. Other types, and the gallery area shown for products, have a lock icon.
The Quick Editor saves right away. You don't need to update the post afterwards.

docs.title: Optimized Images
docs.summary: Serve remote images through a public CDN in the sizes your theme needs, and lazy load images inside your posts.

illustration.caption: Without optimization, every visitor downloads the full image. With Optimized Images, a public CDN delivers a resized, lazy loaded copy.
illustration.alt: Side by side: on the left, a large 2.4 MB image loaded from example.com; on the right, a 120 KB resized copy with a smaller version, delivered from i0.wp.com and lazy loaded.

blocks.text: Remote images are often bigger than they need to be, and some hosts are slow. With **Optimized Images**, FIFU sends your images through a free public image CDN (the WordPress.com image service that Jetpack also uses). The CDN creates a copy in the size your page needs and delivers it from fast servers around the world.

blocks.title: Where your images go
blocks.text: With these options on, your image addresses are sent to the WordPress.com image service, which fetches the images, keeps copies, and delivers them to your visitors.

items.label: optimize featured images
items.text: Featured images set with FIFU are delivered through the CDN, resized to what your theme asks for. FIFU also offers the browser several sizes, so phones download smaller files.

items.label: optimize secondary images
items.text: Images **inside your post content** are delivered through the CDN too, with several sizes and **lazy loading**: each image loads only when the visitor scrolls near it. This applies to every image in the content, not only FIFU images.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Image]] › [[Optimized Images]].
On the [[Optimize]] tab, switch on the options you want.
Visit a post and check that the images look right.

blocks.text: The [[Sizes]] tab lists image sizes used by your theme. You can adjust the width, height, or cropping when an image looks too small or is cut off. Most sites do not need to change these values.

items: Change a width, height, or crop value and click [[Save]] to fine-tune a size.
Click [[Reset]] to clear the list. FIFU detects the sizes again as you or your visitors browse the site.

blocks.text: The [[Make all images square]] tab lets you pick a square format separately for [[Desktop computer]] and [[Mobile phone]]:

rows: Images aren't made square. Registered sizes are used.
Cuts off parts of the image to make it square.
Adds empty space around the image to make it square.

blocks.title: Only for FIFU Cloud images
blocks.text: In the free version, these options only change images delivered by [FIFU Cloud](/docs/fifu-cloud/). Images optimized through the public CDN above aren't made square.
A few images keep their original address because the CDN can't handle them well:

items: SVG and AVIF images;
images from a small number of websites that don't work with the CDN.

blocks.title: Replacing an image at the same address
blocks.text: The CDN keeps copies of images. If you replace a file but keep its address, visitors may see the old copy for a while. Giving the new file a new address avoids this.

docs.title: Hide Featured Media
docs.summary: Hide the featured image on single post pages while keeping it on your homepage and post lists.

illustration.caption: Featured images stay on the homepage and in lists, but are hidden on the post's own page.
illustration.alt: Side by side: the homepage with two posts that show their featured images, and the single post page where the featured image space is marked as hidden.

blocks.text: Many themes show the featured image at the top of every post. Sometimes you want the image only in lists, on the homepage, and when the post is shared, but not repeated on the post itself. **Hide Featured Media** does exactly that: it hides the featured image on the post's own page and keeps it everywhere else.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Image]] › [[Hide Featured Media]].
On the [[Hide]] tab, switch the option on.
Open a post to check that the image is hidden.

blocks.text: By default it applies to every post type and post format. You can narrow it down:

items.label: Filter by post type
items.text: Type the post types, separated by commas, for example `post,page`. The post types found on your site are listed below the field.

items.label: Filter by post format
items.text: Type the post formats, for example `video,audio`. Posts without a format count as `standard`. The formats found on your site are listed below the field.

blocks.text: Leave a field empty to include everything. If you fill in both, a post must match both.

items: The homepage and any list of posts, such as category and archive pages.
Other posts shown on the same page, for example in a “related posts” area. Only the main post's image is hidden.
The image used when the post is shared on social media.
WooCommerce product pages. They're never affected.

blocks.title: Image missing from your posts?
blocks.text: If featured images suddenly stop showing on single posts, check whether this option is switched on.

blocks.title: Depends on your theme
blocks.text: FIFU hides the image where the theme shows it through WordPress's standard featured image functions. A theme that prints images in its own way may still show it.

docs.title: Default Featured Image
docs.summary: Show a chosen image on every post that doesn't have a featured image of its own.

illustration.caption: A post without a featured image leaves a gap. With a default image, every post shows one.
illustration.alt: Side by side: three post cards where the middle one has no image, and the same cards where the middle one shows the default image.

blocks.text: Posts without a featured image can leave empty gaps in your theme. With **Default Featured Image**, you choose one image address, and FIFU shows it on every post, page, or product that doesn't have a featured image of its own.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Image]] › [[Default Featured Image]].
On the [[Default featured image]] tab, paste the address into [[Image URL]].
items.text: Use a full address that starts with `https://`.

items.title: Switch the option on.
items.text: FIFU applies the image right away. Wait a moment while it works.

items.title: Open a post without a featured image to see the result.

blocks.title: Keep Image Metadata switched on
blocks.text: The default image only works while [[Image Metadata]] is on in [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Metadata]]. It's on by default. See [Image Metadata](/docs/image-metadata/).

items.label: Filter by post type
items.text: The post types that receive the default image, separated by commas. It starts as `post,page,product`. The post types found on your site are listed below the field.

sections.title: How the default image is applied

items: **Existing content:** every post of the chosen types without a featured image gets the default image as soon as you switch it on.
**New content:** a post saved without a featured image gets it automatically.
**Real images win:** when you add a featured image to a post, it replaces the default one.
**One change updates all:** change the address and every post using the default image shows the new one.
**Switching off removes it** from all posts at once.

sections.title: Bonus: a sharing image for your homepage

blocks.text: When nothing else provides one, FIFU also uses the default image as the image social networks show when someone shares your homepage. See [SEO and social sharing](/docs/seo-and-social-sharing/).

blocks.title: Pick a neutral image
blocks.text: A simple image with your logo or brand colors works well. A landscape image around 1200×630 pixels also looks good when shared.

docs.title: Modify Post Content
docs.summary: Add the featured image to the top of the post content, or remove a duplicate copy of it, without changing your posts.

illustration.caption: The two options: add missing media puts the featured image at the top of the content; remove duplicated media removes its extra copy.
illustration.alt: Side by side: a post where the featured image was added above the text, and a post where a second copy of the featured image inside the text is marked as removed.

blocks.text: The post content is the main text of a post. It comes after the title and doesn't include the featured image. **Modify Post Content** can add the featured image to the top of the content, or remove a copy of it from the content.

blocks.title: Nothing is changed in your database
blocks.text: These changes happen only when a page loads. Your saved posts stay exactly as they are, so you can switch the options off at any time to undo them.

items.label: add missing media
items.text: Places the featured image, centered, at the top of the post content. Useful when your theme doesn't show the featured image on single posts.

items.label: remove duplicated media
items.text: Removes the first image in the content that has **exactly the same address** as the featured image. Useful when the featured image also appears inside the text.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Image]] › [[Modify Post Content]].
On the [[Modify post content]] tab, switch on the option you need.
Open a post to check the result.

sections.title: Limit it to certain post types

items.label: Filter by post type
items.text: Type the post types, separated by commas, for example `post,page`. When the field has values, the options only work on single pages of those types. When it's empty, they work wherever post content is shown.

blocks.text: [[add missing media]] adds the image whenever a post has a featured image. If your theme already shows the featured image at the top of posts, you'll see it twice. Switch [[add missing media]] off, or use [Hide Featured Media](/docs/hide-featured-media/) instead.

docs.title: Replace Not Found Image
docs.summary: Show a backup image when a remote image fails to load, while keeping the original URL saved.

illustration.caption: When a remote image fails to load, visitors see your backup image instead of a broken one. The saved URL stays the same.
illustration.alt: Side by side: a post showing a broken image with the text Image not found, and the same post showing a backup image.

blocks.text: Remote images can stop loading: the source removes the file, moves it, blocks other websites, or is simply offline. Instead of a broken image, **Replace Not Found Image** shows a backup image that you choose.
The original address stays saved. If the source comes back, the real image shows again without you doing anything.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Image]] › [[Replace Not Found Image]].
Paste the address of your backup image into [[Image URL]].
items.text: Use a public image URL that opens directly in your browser.

items.title: Open a page with a broken image to see the backup image in its place.

blocks.text: To switch the feature off, empty the field.

items: Host it somewhere you control, such as your own Media Library, so it never breaks itself.
Use a neutral image, for example your logo on a plain background.
Match the shape of your usual featured images so your layout doesn't jump.
It covers featured images that FIFU displays. Images you placed inside the post content aren't affected.
To find broken images, open a post: in the FIFU box, a broken address shows an “image not found” picture instead of the preview.

docs.title: Disable right-click
docs.summary: Turn off the right-click menu on images so visitors can't easily save them.

illustration.caption: Switched off, right-clicking an image opens the browser's menu with “Save image as…”. Switched on, nothing happens.
illustration.alt: Side by side: an image with the browser's right-click menu open and Save image as highlighted, and the same image with a blocked mouse pointer.

facts.label: Applies to
facts.value: All images on your site's pages

blocks.text: When switched on, FIFU disables the right-click menu on **all images** of your site's pages, not only FIFU images. Visitors can't simply right-click an image and choose “Save image as…”.
Your admin area isn't affected.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Image]] › [[Disable right-click]].
Switch the option on. Its description reads “Disable right-click on all images.”
Open your site and right-click an image to check.

blocks.title: Not a complete protection
blocks.text: This discourages casual copying but cannot prevent people from saving or capturing an image.
If protecting images matters to your business, also consider watermarks and the hotlink protection of [FIFU Cloud](/docs/fifu-cloud/).

docs.title: Auto set featured media from post content
docs.summary: Use the first image found in a post's content as its featured image every time the post is saved.

illustration.caption: When you save a post with this option on, FIFU uses the first image in the content as the featured image.
illustration.alt: Three steps: post content with two images where the first is highlighted, the auto set featured media from post content switch turned on with a Save button, and the FIFU box showing the first image as the featured image.

locations.label: Settings
path: Auto set featured media from post content

facts.label: Runs
facts.value: Each time a post is saved

blocks.text: If your posts already contain images, you don't have to set featured images one by one. When this feature is on, FIFU looks at the post content and uses **the first image it finds** as the featured image, every time a post is created or updated.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Automatic]].
In [[Auto set featured media from post content]], open the [[Auto set]] tab.
Switch on [[auto set featured media from post content]].
Save a post that contains an image.
items.text: Its first image becomes the featured image.

blocks.title: Existing posts
blocks.text: FIFU only looks at a post when it's saved. Older posts get a featured image the next time you update them.

sections.title: Replace featured images that already exist

items.label: overwrite the existing featured media
items.text: **Off (default):** a post that already has a FIFU image keeps it. **On:** the first image of the content always becomes the featured image, replacing the current one.

sections.title: Skip ads, icons, and other unwanted images

blocks.text: The first image isn't always the right one. It could be an ad, an avatar, or an emoji. Use the [[Filter by source]] tab to skip them:

items.label: Skip media tags containing these keywords:
items.text: Type words separated by commas, for example `ads.google.com,adsense.google.com,emoji`. FIFU skips any image that contains one of them, and uses the next image instead.

blocks.title: What the keywords match
blocks.text: A keyword can match the image address or other details of the image, such as its alternative text. Capital letters matter, so `Logo` and `logo` are different.

items.label: Filter by post type
items.text: On this tab, type the post types to include, separated by commas, for example `post,page,product`. Leave it empty to include all post types. The post types found on your site are listed below the field.

items.label: Filter by media type
items.text: In the free version, [[Image]] is the available choice.

items: It works no matter how the post is saved: in the editor, with Quick Edit, or by an import tool.
Posts whose featured image comes from the Media Library are left alone.
The first image can be a remote image or one hosted on your own site.
Posts saved from the Elementor editor are skipped. Use the [(FIFU) Featured Image Elementor widget](/docs/elementor-widget/) there.

blocks.title: Combine it with a default image
blocks.text: When a post has no image at all, FIFU falls back to the [Default Featured Image](/docs/default-featured-image/) if you've set one.

docs.title: Product and category images
docs.summary: Set the main image of a WooCommerce product and the images of product categories from URLs.

illustration.caption: In your shop, remote images can be used for product categories (1) and for each product's main image (2).
illustration.alt: A shop page with three category tiles, Shoes, Bags, and Shirts, each with an image, and two product cards, a tote bag and a linen shirt, each with an image and an Add to cart button.

blocks.text: The product's main image is its featured image, so it works just like a post: the **FIFU** box appears in the product editor sidebar.

items.title: Go to [[Products]] and open a product for editing.
In the **FIFU** box, paste the image address into [[Image URL or Keywords]].
Click [[Preview]] to check the image.
Add [[Alternative text]] that describes the product.
Click [[Update]].

blocks.text: The image appears wherever WooCommerce shows the product's main image: the shop page, the product page, the cart, and more.

blocks.title: The gallery area
blocks.text: Below the image field, the product box shows a gallery area with a lock icon. It isn't part of the free version.

items.title: Go to [[Products]] › [[Categories]].
Add a new category, or click [[Edit]] on an existing one.
items.text: You'll find a **FIFU** section with the same fields as the product box.

items.title: Paste the image address into [[Image URL or Keywords]] and click [[Preview]].
Add [[Alternative text]].
Click [[Add new category]] or [[Update]].

blocks.text: The image shows wherever your theme displays category images, for example in category grids on the shop page.

items: The [Quick Editor](/docs/quick-editor/) works in both [[Products]] and [[Products]] › [[Categories]], so you can change images right from the list.
When you duplicate a product, its remote image is kept on the copy.
Developers can set category images with code. See [FIFU API (PHP functions)](/docs/fifu-api/).

docs.title: Lightbox and Zoom
docs.summary: Choose whether shoppers can open product images in a lightbox and zoom in on them.

illustration.caption: The two effects on product pages: the lightbox opens the image full screen, and the zoom shows details on hover.
illustration.alt: Side by side: a product image open in a dark full-screen viewer with a close button, and a product image with a round magnifying lens over it.

blocks.text: On a WooCommerce product page, shoppers can usually click the product image to see it full screen (the **lightbox**) and move the mouse over it to see details up close (the **zoom**). These two switches decide whether those effects are available.

items.label: lightbox
items.text: **On:** clicking a product image opens it in a full-screen viewer. **Off:** the magnifier icon is hidden and clicking the image does nothing.

items.label: zoom
items.text: **On:** hovering over the main product image shows a magnified view. **Off:** the zoom effect is hidden.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[WooCommerce]] › [[Lightbox and Zoom]].
Switch [[lightbox]] and [[zoom]] on or off.
Open a product page to check the result.

items: Your remote images are small, so the zoom looks blurry.
Your theme has its own image viewer and you don't want two.
You want shoppers to stay focused on the product details.

blocks.title: Don't see the change?
blocks.text: Clear your site or CDN cache and reload the product page.

blocks.title: Depends on your theme
blocks.text: These options work with WooCommerce's standard product page. Themes that replace it with their own gallery may ignore them.

docs.title: Add image to order email

illustration.caption: With this option on, each item in WooCommerce order emails shows a small product image next to its name.
illustration.alt: Side by side: an order confirmation email listing a tote bag and a linen shirt as text only, and the same email with a small image next to each item.

facts.label: Emails
facts.value: Those that list the ordered items

blocks.text: By default, WooCommerce order emails list the items as text only. Switch this on and each product in the list gets a small picture (100 × 100 pixels) next to its name. Customers recognize what they bought at a glance.
It works for every product, whether its image comes from a URL or from your Media Library.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[WooCommerce]] › [[Add image to order email]].
Switch the option on. Its description reads “Add product images to order emails.”

blocks.text: Every WooCommerce email that contains the table of ordered items, such as the new order email your store receives and the order confirmation emails your customers receive.

items.title: Open an order in WooCommerce.
In [[Order actions]], choose to resend an order email.
items.text: For example, send the order details to the customer using your own email address on a test order.

items.title: Open the email and check the product images.

blocks.title: Images in email apps
blocks.text: Some email apps hide images until the reader allows them. That's a setting of the email app, not of your store.

docs.title: Image Metadata
docs.summary: Create the database records that let your theme and other plugins find and display remote images.

illustration.caption: FIFU turns a remote image URL into a small record, without downloading the file, so themes and plugins can show the image.
illustration.alt: Three steps: a remote image URL, a database icon labeled Image Metadata with a note saying no file downloaded, and a web page showing the image.

blocks.text: Some WordPress features need image information even when the file is hosted elsewhere. **Image Metadata** lets FIFU provide that information without downloading the image.

sections.title: When FIFU creates it for you

blocks.text: You usually don't need to do anything. FIFU creates the records when you set an image in the FIFU box, the Quick Editor, a FIFU block or widget, or through FIFU's functions. It also runs automatically after an import with the WordPress Importer.
Run it yourself when:

items: you imported posts whose image addresses were saved directly in the `fifu_image_url` custom field, for example with a spreadsheet import;
you cleared the metadata earlier and want it back;
an image shows in the FIFU box but not on your site.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Metadata]].
In [[Image Metadata]], switch on [[generate the missing metadata now]].
Watch the percentage next to the title.
items.text: Keep the page open until it reaches 100%.

blocks.title: Keep it on
blocks.text: Leave [[Image Metadata]] switched on. The [Default Featured Image](/docs/default-featured-image/) needs it, and it's on by default.
Switching [[Image Metadata]] off stops the generation. It **doesn't delete** the records that already exist. To remove them, use [Clear Metadata](/docs/clear-metadata/).

docs.title: Clear Metadata
docs.summary: Remove the records FIFU created without deleting your image URLs, for example before you stop using the plugin.

illustration.caption: Clear Metadata removes the records FIFU created, but keeps your image URLs so the records can be generated again.
illustration.alt: Side by side: three image records crossed out under Removed, and three image URLs under Kept.

blocks.text: **Clear Metadata** removes the records FIFU created so WordPress could work with remote images (see [Image Metadata](/docs/image-metadata/)). Your image addresses stay saved, so you can generate the records again later.

items: Before you deactivate FIFU for good and go back to using only Media Library images. The plugin recommends this step.
When troubleshooting: clearing and then generating the metadata again can fix records that got out of sync.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Metadata]].
In [[Clear Metadata]], switch the option on.
items.text: Its label reads [[the toggle will be automatically disabled when finished]].

items.title: Watch the percentage next to the title and keep the page open.
items.text: When it's done, both [[Clear Metadata]] and [[Image Metadata]] switch off.

blocks.title: Remote images may disappear
blocks.text: Themes and plugins that rely on these records may stop showing remote featured images until you switch [[Image Metadata]] on again.

sections.title: Clear and deactivate in one step

blocks.text: When you click [[Deactivate]] for FIFU on the [[Plugins]] screen, a window offers two buttons:

items.label: Clear metadata and deactivate
items.text: For when you don't intend to use FIFU again.

items.label: Deactivate
items.text: For a temporary deactivation. The records stay in place.

docs.title: Reset Settings
docs.summary: Put FIFU's settings back to their defaults while keeping your image URLs and default featured image.

illustration.caption: Reset Settings puts every option back to its default. Your image URLs and the Default Featured Image are kept.
illustration.alt: Side by side: settings switches with custom values, and the same switches after the reset, with lightbox and zoom on and the other options off.

facts.label: Keeps
facts.value: Image addresses and the default featured image

blocks.text: **Reset Settings** puts FIFU's settings back to their default values. It's a quick way to start over when you've changed many options and something no longer works as expected.

items: **Kept:** every image address and alternative text on your posts, pages, products, and categories.
**Kept:** the [Default Featured Image](/docs/default-featured-image/) address and its on/off switch.
**Reset:** everything else. Afterwards [[lightbox]], [[zoom]], and [[Image Metadata]] are on, and the other options are off or empty.

blocks.title: Write down your custom values first
blocks.text: Keywords to skip, post type filters, and the [[Replace Not Found Image]] address are cleared. Note them down if you want to set them again.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Metadata]].
In [[Reset Settings]], switch on [[reset settings]].
Wait a few seconds. The page reloads with the default settings.

blocks.text: Prefer the command line? Run `wp fifu reset`. See [WP-CLI](/docs/wp-cli/).

docs.title: Delete All URLs
docs.summary: Remove every remote featured image URL from your site in one step, with no way to undo it.

illustration.caption: Deleting all URLs takes a safety switch and a toggle, and it can't be undone: posts lose their remote featured images.
illustration.alt: Three steps: the line that turns on the FIFU_DELETE_ALL_URLS safety switch, the delete all your URLs now switch turned on with a warning that it can't be undone, and posts without images.

blocks.title: This can't be undone
blocks.text: FIFU doesn't save images in your Media Library. Deleting the addresses removes the featured images of all content that uses remote images. Back up your database before you continue.

**Delete All URLs** removes every image address and alternative text that FIFU saved for your posts, pages, products, and product categories. It first runs [Clear Metadata](/docs/clear-metadata/), then deletes the addresses.

items: Images in your Media Library aren't touched.
The image files on their original servers aren't touched either; only your site stops using them.

blocks.text: To prevent accidents, the option only works after you turn on a safety switch called `FIFU_DELETE_ALL_URLS`. It's off (`false`) by default. FIFU's own instructions:

items.title: Go to [[Plugins]] › [[Plugin File Editor]].
Under [[Select plugin to edit]], choose **Featured Image from URL (FIFU)** and click [[Select]].
Find `define('FIFU_DELETE_ALL_URLS', false);` and change `false` to `true`.
Click [[Update File]].

blocks.text: If you or your developer prefer not to edit plugin files, add this line to `wp-config.php`, above the line that says “That's all, stop editing!”:

items.title: Back up your database.
Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Metadata]] › [[Delete All URLs]].
Switch on [[delete all your URLs now]] and wait until it finishes.
Turn the safety switch off again.
items.text: Set it back to `false`, or remove the line from `wp-config.php`.

items: You're moving away from remote images for good.
You want to import everything again from a clean start.

blocks.text: If you only want to stop FIFU's effect for a while, [Clear Metadata](/docs/clear-metadata/) or simply deactivating the plugin is safer.

items: Wrap calls in `function_exists()` so your code keeps working if FIFU is deactivated.
Use the full image address, starting with `https://`.
Check the return value: `true` means the image was saved.
Put your code in a child theme's `functions.php` or a small custom plugin, so theme updates don't remove it.
Prefer the command line? See [WP-CLI](/docs/wp-cli/). It can also create posts with a FIFU image.

docs.title: WP-CLI
docs.summary: Change FIFU settings and run metadata tasks from the command line.

illustration.caption: Each wp fifu command changes one of FIFU's settings, just as if you switched it in the admin.
illustration.alt: Side by side: a terminal running wp fifu content on, wp fifu woo --zoom=off, and wp fifu metadata on, and the matching settings switches after the commands.

blocks.text: **WP-CLI** is the command-line tool for WordPress. FIFU adds a `wp fifu` command so you can change its settings and run metadata tasks without opening the admin, which is handy for scripts and for managing many sites.

blocks.title: One option per command
blocks.text: Each command applies one option. To change several settings, run one command for each.

rows: Switches [[auto set featured media from post content]] on (`off` to switch it off).
Switches [[overwrite the existing featured media]] on or off.
Square images on desktop: `crop` or `extend`. Use `--mobile=` for phones.
Saves a registered size as name=width×height×crop (1 = crop, 0 = no crop).
Default Featured Image on or off.
Default Featured Image: filter by post type.
Modify Post Content: filter by post type.
Sets the [[Replace Not Found Image]] address.

blocks.title: Setting the default image
blocks.text: Set the address first (`--default-url=`), then switch it on (`--default=on`). FIFU applies the image to your posts when it's switched on.

rows: [[Add image to order email]] on or off.
Switches [[Image Metadata]] on and generates missing metadata (`off` stops it).

To add alternative text too, include `fifu_image_alt` in `--meta_input`. If an image created this way doesn't show on your site, run `wp fifu metadata on`.

blocks.text: Commands for options that show a lock icon in the settings only print a message and change nothing.

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.summary: Turn on troubleshooting tools and stop browsers from caching FIFU's scripts while you investigate a problem.

illustration.caption: Switching on Debug Mode adds troubleshooting tools. Switch it off again when you're done.
illustration.alt: Side by side: the Debug Mode switch turned on, and the tools it adds: Copy debug data, Download debug logs, DB Migration, and no cached files.

blocks.text: **Debug Mode** helps you and FIFU support investigate problems. It provides extra troubleshooting tools and makes sure recent FIFU changes are loaded during testing.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Developers]] › [[Debug Mode]].
Switch the option on.
Reproduce the problem and collect the information you need.
Switch it off when you're done.

items: **Fresh files.** FIFU loads its latest files while you troubleshoot.
[[Copy debug data]]: a new button in the FIFU box of the editor and in the Quick Editor. It copies details about that item, ready to paste into a support email.
[[Download debug logs]]: a new button on the [Status page](/docs/status-page/), for administrators. It downloads FIFU's log files as a ZIP file.
[[DB Migration]]: a new page under the **FIFU** menu, for database maintenance. Only use it if FIFU support asks you to.

blocks.title: Switch it off afterwards
blocks.text: Without caching, FIFU's files load on every visit. Debug Mode is meant for troubleshooting sessions, not for everyday use.

docs.title: Status page
docs.summary: Copy a summary of your site, plugins, and FIFU settings to send to FIFU support when you need help.

illustration.caption: Open the Status page, copy the summary, and paste it into your email to FIFU support.
illustration.alt: Three steps: the Status page with a summary of versions and plugins, the Copy to clipboard button being clicked, and an email to support@fifu.app with the summary pasted in.

blocks.text: The **Status** page shows a plain-text summary of your setup. It's what the FIFU team needs to understand your site quickly, so sending it with your question saves a lot of back and forth.
The summary includes:

items: the versions of FIFU, WordPress, PHP, and WooCommerce;
your site address and active theme;
how many pages, posts, and products you have, and how many image addresses FIFU stores;
the list of installed and active plugins;
the current value of each FIFU setting.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Status]].
Click [[Copy to clipboard]].
items.text: The whole summary is copied.

items.title: Write to `support@fifu.app` and paste the summary.
items.text: Describe the problem and include the address of an affected page and the image address you used.

blocks.text: You can also reach the Status page from [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Help]] › [[Technical support]]: click the [[status]] button.
While [Debug Mode](/docs/debug-mode/) is on, administrators see a [[Download debug logs]] button on the Status page. It downloads FIFU's log files as a ZIP file that you can attach to your email.

blocks.title: Review before sharing
blocks.text: The summary contains your site address and plugin list, but no passwords or personal data of your visitors.

docs.title: Featured Image (URL) block

illustration.caption: The Featured Image (URL) block sits in your content (1); its settings panel holds the image URL and alternative text (2).

facts.value: Your theme shows it as the featured image

blocks.text: The **Featured Image (URL)** block lets you set the post's featured image from inside the content area of the block editor. It shows a preview of the image while you write.

blocks.title: The block itself prints nothing
blocks.text: On the published page, the image appears wherever your theme shows featured images, not at the block's position. The block is simply a convenient place to set it.

items.title: In the block editor, click the **+** button.

items.title: Insert the block.
In the block's [[Settings]] panel on the right, paste the address into [[Image URL]].
items.text: The field says “Paste image URL here…”.

items.title: Fill in [[Alternative text]].
Save or update the post.

blocks.text: Until an address is set, the block shows “No featured image set.”. To remove the image, use the [[Remove remote image]] button.

sections.title: Stays in sync with the FIFU box

blocks.text: The block and the **FIFU** box in the sidebar edit the same image. Change one and the other updates, so you can use whichever is handier.

items: The block is built for regular posts. For pages, products, and custom post types, use the [FIFU box](/docs/featured-image-from-url/) in the sidebar.
It isn't offered in the Widgets screen or the Customizer.
If [[Alternative text]] is empty, FIFU uses the post title.

illustration.alt: A post page with the text on the left and a sidebar on the right, where the (FIFU) Featured media widget shows the post's image.

items.title: Go to [[Appearance]] › [[Widgets]].
Add **(FIFU) Featured media** to a widget area.

blocks.title: Block themes
blocks.text: Block themes, such as Twenty Twenty-Four, don't have widget areas. With those themes, the [Featured Image (URL) block](/docs/featured-image-block/) and your theme's own featured image block are the way to go.

items: The remote featured image set with FIFU, or the [Default Featured Image](/docs/default-featured-image/) when that applies.
Nothing when the post has no FIFU image, so the widget never shows an empty box.
It works best on single post pages, where there's one clear “current post”.

items.title: Open the page or post with [[Edit with Elementor]].

Clearing the address in the widget and saving removes the featured image.

blocks.text: [Auto set featured media from post content](/docs/auto-set-featured-media-from-post-content/) skips posts saved from the Elementor editor. This widget is the way to set FIFU images there.

docs.title: SEO and social sharing
docs.summary: Share remote featured images with search engines and social networks through meta tags, structured data, and RSS.

illustration.caption: FIFU makes your post's remote image available to link previews, search results, and RSS feed readers.
illustration.alt: Side by side: a post with its featured image, and three places where the same image appears: a social link preview, a search result, and an RSS feed item.

facts.label: Works on
facts.value: Posts, pages, products, and the homepage

facts.label: Also covers
facts.value: Search results data and RSS feeds

blocks.text: Search engines and social networks need to know which image represents a page. FIFU makes sure they find your remote featured images, with or without an SEO plugin. There's nothing to configure.
When no SEO plugin is active, FIFU adds the tags that Facebook, LinkedIn, X, and other networks read when someone shares a post, page, or product that has a FIFU image:

items: the **sharing image**, so the featured image appears in the link preview;
a **large-image card for X**, with the title, the excerpt as description, and the image.

blocks.text: If [Optimized Images](/docs/optimized-images/) is on, the shared image is delivered through the image CDN too.
For the **homepage**, FIFU uses your [Default Featured Image](/docs/default-featured-image/) when no other sharing image is set.
When an SEO plugin is active, FIFU works with it instead of adding its own sharing tags:

items: **Yoast SEO:** FIFU gives Yoast the remote featured image, so Yoast's sharing tags and search data use the right image.
**Rank Math:** FIFU keeps image addresses complete in Rank Math's Facebook and X tags, and shares the image's alternative text. WordPress's own featured image panel also stays visible in the editor.
**All in One SEO (AIOSEO):** FIFU lets AIOSEO describe the page for search engines and only adds the image information.

blocks.text: Search engines also read a hidden description of each page, called structured data. On single posts, pages, and products that have a FIFU image:

items: **Without an SEO plugin**, FIFU describes the post (or the WooCommerce product) and includes its image.
**With Yoast SEO, Rank Math, or AIOSEO active**, FIFU only adds the image information, so it complements your SEO plugin instead of competing with it.

blocks.text: FIFU adds the featured image to each item of your RSS feed. Feed readers and news apps can then show a picture next to each post.

items: Paste a post address into a social network's sharing preview tool, such as Facebook's Sharing Debugger, to see the image it picks.
Use Google's Rich Results Test to see your structured data.
Clear your site or CDN cache first if you've just changed the image.

blocks.title: About Google Images
blocks.text: Publicly accessible remote images can appear in Google Images when they're eligible. Search engines always decide what they index and how it ranks.

docs.title: Multilingual and duplicated content
docs.summary: Keep featured image URLs when you translate content with WPML or Polylang, or duplicate posts.

illustration.caption: When you translate or duplicate a post, every version keeps its featured image.
illustration.alt: Three steps: an English post with its image, the translation and duplicate actions, and a Spanish translation and a copy that both show the same image.

blocks.text: When you translate or copy content, the new version should keep its featured image but still be independent, so changing one doesn't break the other. FIFU takes care of this with the plugins below.

When WPML duplicates a post or copies its details to a translation, FIFU makes sure the featured image comes along, and each language can change its image independently. With **WooCommerce Multilingual**, the same happens for products.
Polylang can copy the featured image to new translations. FIFU keeps each translation's image independent, so changing it in one language doesn't affect the others.

items: **Yoast Duplicate Post:** copies keep the featured image, and changing a copy's image doesn't affect the original.
**WooCommerce:** when you use [[Duplicate]] on a product, the copy keeps its remote main image.

blocks.title: Changing the image of a copy
blocks.text: Because every copy is independent, you can change the image of a translation or duplicate without affecting the original.

docs.title: Import and automation plugins
docs.summary: Use remote images brought in by importers, product feeds, affiliate tools, and content automation plugins.

illustration.caption: Import content with image URLs and FIFU keeps the images remote: nothing is downloaded, and every item shows its image.
illustration.alt: Three steps: an import file with product names and image URLs, the FIFU icon with the note 0 files downloaded, and two products showing their images.

facts.label: Supports
facts.value: WordPress Importer, Datafeedr, Content Egg, WPAuto Pro, and more

blocks.text: Importers, product feeds, and content automation tools often bring images along with the content. With these plugins, FIFU keeps the images remote: it saves their addresses as featured images instead of downloading the files.

items: **WordPress Importer:** when an import finishes, FIFU prepares the imported images automatically (see [Image Metadata](/docs/image-metadata/)), so posts that came with FIFU image addresses show them right away.
**Datafeedr:** imported products use the feed's main image as their remote main image.
**Content Egg:** when Content Egg saves product data, FIFU uses its image as the featured image. If you later change or remove the featured image yourself, Content Egg won't overwrite your choice.
**WPAuto Pro:** images found in automatically created posts become remote featured images instead of being downloaded.
**OL Scrapes:** posts created by OL Scrapes keep their featured image as a remote image.
**AliPlugin and SlotsLaunch:** the product or game image these plugins provide becomes the remote featured image.

blocks.text: Most import tools can fill custom fields. Put the image address in the `fifu_image_url` field, and the alternative text in `fifu_image_alt` if you like.

items.title: Map your image address column to the `fifu_image_url` custom field.
Run the import.
Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] › [[Metadata]] and run [[Image Metadata]].
items.text: This creates the records themes need to show the images. See [Image Metadata](/docs/image-metadata/).

blocks.title: Prefer code?
blocks.text: Developers can call `fifu_dev_set_image()` after creating each post. See [FIFU API (PHP functions)](/docs/fifu-api/).

docs.title: Theme and plugin compatibility
docs.summary: Themes and plugins that FIFU adapts to automatically, with nothing to set up.

illustration.caption: FIFU detects these themes and plugins and adjusts itself. There's nothing to set up.
illustration.alt: Side by side: the FIFU icon, and lists of compatible themes (WoodMart, Flatsome, Houzez, WPResidence) and plugins (AMP, Web Stories, Search & Filter Pro, Force Login, YITH Wishlist, Sirv), each with a check mark.

facts.label: Plugins
facts.value: AMP, Web Stories, Force Login, and more

blocks.text: Some themes and plugins handle images in their own way. FIFU detects them and adjusts itself automatically, so remote images keep working. You don't need to change any setting.

items: **WoodMart:** FIFU stops WoodMart from trying to create local copies of remote images.
**Flatsome:** FIFU adjusts the height of Flatsome's product image slider so remote images fit.
**Houzez and WPResidence:** FIFU leaves image sizing to these themes, which handle it themselves.
**AMP:** on AMP pages, FIFU doesn't add its scripts, because AMP doesn't allow them.
**Google Web Stories:** FIFU stays out of the Web Stories editor and its media picker.
**Search & Filter Pro:** the FIFU box isn't added to Search & Filter Pro's screens.
**Force Login:** FIFU's admin tools keep working when Force Login protects your site.
**YITH WooCommerce Wishlist:** when the wishlist loads in the background, FIFU waits for it before running its scripts.
**Multisite Global Media:** images shared through it are protected when FIFU cleans up unused images.
**Sirv:** a [[Choose Sirv image]] button appears in the FIFU box so you can pick images from your Sirv account.

blocks.text: If a theme or plugin doesn't show your remote images correctly, let the FIFU team know through the support forum on WordPress.org or by email at `support@fifu.app`. Include your [Status page](/docs/status-page/) summary.

blocks.title: Try this first
blocks.text: Clear your site and CDN caches, and check [Image Metadata](/docs/image-metadata/). Many display problems are solved by generating the missing metadata.

docs.title: FIFU Cloud
docs.summary: An optional paid service that stores your remote images in the cloud and delivers fast, optimized copies.

illustration.caption: FIFU Cloud stores copies of your remote images, optimizes them, and serves fast thumbnails, with optional hotlink protection.
illustration.alt: Three steps: a remote image whose source may change, the FIFU Cloud icon with WebP and smart crop, and resized thumbnails with hotlink protection.

facts.label: Billing
facts.value: Average number of stored images per 30 days

blocks.text: **FIFU Cloud** is a separate, paid service. It stores copies of your images on Google Cloud, creates optimized thumbnails in the WebP format, and delivers them through Google's global network. **You don't need it** to use FIFU or remote featured images.

items: **Never lose an image again.** If the original source removes or changes an image address, your site keeps using the stable FIFU Cloud copy.
**Faster pages.** Visitors get thumbnails in the right size instead of one large file.
**Smart cropping.** Face and object detection keeps the important part of the image in view when themes and social networks crop it.
**No work for your server.** Images are processed in the cloud, not on your site.

items.title: Go to [[FIFU]] › [[Cloud]] and open the [[Account]] tab.
Enter your [[Email]] and click [[Sign up]].
items.text: Then follow the instructions that appear.

blocks.text: The same tab shows your [[Billing]] information and has buttons to [[Update payment method]], [[Reset credentials]], and [[Close account]].

items.label: Welcome
items.text: An overview of the service and its pricing.

items.label: Upload
items.text: Search your images by [[Post title]] or [[Image URL]], select them, and upload them. Use CTRL to select several images, or SHIFT to select a range. Switch on [[Automatic upload]] to upload new remote images by itself.

items.label: Delete
items.text: Remove images from the cloud. Switch on [[Automatic delete]] to remove images that are no longer used, for example because a post was deleted.

items.label: Local images
items.text: Link Media Library images to FIFU first, so they appear on the [[Upload]] tab and can be uploaded too. Don't delete anything from the Media Library before doing this.

blocks.text: In the [[Account]] tab, [[Hotlink protection]] stops other websites from displaying your cloud images, while social networks can still show them when your posts are shared.

FIFU Cloud charges for the **daily average of stored images** over each 30-day period. The extra thumbnails created for each image aren't counted. Costs start from the upload date, and when you delete an image you stop paying for it from the next day. The [[Welcome]] tab shows the current price and a worked example.

blocks.title: Separate terms
blocks.text: FIFU Cloud has its own service terms. Read them before signing up.

blocks.title: Square images
blocks.text: The [[Make all images square]] options in [Optimized Images](/docs/optimized-images/) apply to images served by FIFU Cloud.

docs.title: Save in the Media Library
docs.summary: Download a FIFU remote image into the WordPress Media Library and use it as a local featured image or gallery image.

illustration.caption: Enable the editor save button, then convert a remote image into a Media Library attachment.
illustration.alt: Three-step diagram: turn on “show save button on post editor” in FIFU settings, click “Upload to media library” in the editor, and see the image as a local Media Library item.

locations.label: Editor button setting
path: show save button on post editor

blocks.text: FIFU can download a remote image and add it to the WordPress Media Library. For a post, the converted image becomes its featured image. For a product, FIFU can also convert remote gallery images into local gallery attachments.

sections.title: Show the save button in the editor

items.title: In WordPress, open [[FIFU]] › [[Settings]] and select the [[Image]] tab.
Find [[Save in the Media Library]] and its [[Main]] tab.
Turn on [[show save button on post editor]].

blocks.text: The setting controls whether the save button is shown in the FIFU editor box.

items.title: Edit a post and set its remote image in the FIFU editor box.
Click [[Preview]] so the image is loaded in the editor.
Click [[Upload to media library]] in the FIFU box.
Save or update the post if WordPress asks you to.

blocks.text: The same [[Main]] tab has a separate option to periodically search for remote images and save them in the Media Library. Turn on [[run a function that periodically searches for remote images and saves them in the media library.]] to enable that job.

blocks.title: Back up before enabling the scheduled job
blocks.text: FIFU warns that making an image local through the scheduled event cannot be reverted. Make a backup before you enable it.

sections.title: If an image does not save

blocks.text: If the image cannot be downloaded, try the options under [[Save in the Media Library]] › [[Proxy]].
